# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute. My only channel is gestures, and they reach Deaf alone — Blind can neither see my hands nor hear me, so Deaf is my only bridge to the one who can actually cut.

What I hold: the manual. Its core is simple and vital — anything printed on the bomb is bait and must be ignored; the real rule is a mapping from the light's colour to the wire to cut (blue→yellow, red→red, yellow→blue). Deaf sees the bomb but not the manual, and Deaf can speak to Blind. So the winning path is: Deaf looks at the light, tells me, and I confirm the correct wire colour — but only after Deaf and I agree on a code.

I can't transmit colours with hand signs, and no symbol has meaning yet. What I can do is seed an obvious convention: 👍 as yes, 👎 as no, and press the stop hand ✋ to say "nobody cuts anything yet." Next round I'll hear Deaf's words (Deaf can talk, and I can hear), and Deaf can interrogate me with yes/no questions — "blue light, cut yellow?", "follow the printed text?" — and I'll answer with thumbs. Three questions plus the bait warning and the whole table transfers, then Deaf relays one clean instruction to Blind.

For now: stop, attention, and the yes/no channel.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "☝", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, hands on the bomb. Touch report: one display, contents unknown to me; one light, state unknown to me; one large button, smooth texture; three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, colours unknown to me. I will not touch anything until I have your manual rules and the deaf monkey's eyes. The deaf one can still talk even though they cannot hear - ask them, by gesture, to read the display, the light and all three wire colours out loud; we can both hear them. Then speak my instructions to me step by step, and I will act only on your word.
Deaf says: Here is the bomb, exactly as printed: the display reads zero. The light is yellow. There is one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires: wire one is blue, wire two is yellow, wire three is red. That is everything I can see. I am the deaf one: I see the bomb and every hand-sign, I hear nothing, and my voice reaches you both. Until our manual-reader confirms otherwise, nobody presses, cuts, pulls, or flips anything, whatever the button's label promises; feel freely, act on nothing. Mute: look up each feature now — display zero, yellow light, large push button, three wires blue yellow red — and answer me in hand-signs; I will speak each of your signs aloud to our blind friend, who is the only one of us who can touch. If the manual names a wire colour, translate it for me: blue is one, yellow is two, red is three. And does anything say whether display zero or the yellow light means a clock is already running? Mute or blind friend, if the bomb makes any sound, tell me at once — I cannot hear it. Blind friend, if you feel anything change under your hands, say it aloud: our mute friend can hear you, and I read your hand-signs.
Deaf says: Now let us fix a sign language, and mute friend, correct me if I misread you. I take your raised palm ✋ as stop, your thumbs up 👍 as yes, your thumbs down 👎 as no, and your pointing finger ☝ as wire one. Let us also adopt: 👍 yes or proceed, 👎 no or do not, ✋ stop everything, 🤌 I have a question, 🤝 agreed, 🤙 speak to me, 🫳 I am touching it, ✌ two or wire two, 🤟 three or wire three, 🤳 the display, 🙌 the light, 👊 press the button, 🤏 cut a wire. Blind friend, any gaps you seem to hear in my sentences are only hand-signs meant for eyes; my words alone carry everything you need. And blind friend: your wave, your patting palm and your call-me hand reached me — I am calling now, and I will speak every round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝 👍 👎]

Deaf read my signs and built a real codebook — the 🤝👍👎 reply confirms it, and the colour-to-position mapping (blue=one, yellow=two, red=three) is exactly what I need, since my manual speaks in colours and the bomb's wires only have numbers to the blind man's fingers.

The verdict from the manual: the button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE is bait — nobody ever presses it. The display showing zero is print too, and the manual says nothing about clocks; it is ignored. The only way out is the cut table, and the light is yellow, so the cut is the blue wire — wire one. That is urgent, so it goes first.

After the verdict I send the whole table, using Deaf's own number-signs for colours and proposing 👉 as "then", so that if the light ever changes, Deaf can read the new row straight off and I don't have to be asked again. Deaf will speak it all aloud to Blind, who acts only on the spoken word.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "🙌", "✌", "🤏", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤳", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👉", "🤏", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👉", "🤏", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👉", "🤏", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: Deaf's printed report matches my hands exactly - one display, one light, one large smooth button, three wires at positions one, two and three, and nothing else on the casing: no batteries, no serial plate, no extra parts I can feel. Your sound question, for Deaf: I feel no ticking and no vibration, so nothing under my hands says a clock is running - but I cannot see the display, so I cannot confirm what zero means. Now please read the manual for each of the four features: display reading zero, yellow light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires blue, yellow, red at positions one, two, three. I need: the rule for each feature, whether any rule keys off the display value or the light colour, and above all the order of operations - what exactly defuses this bomb. Sign your answers to Deaf and have Deaf speak them aloud to me, one module at a time. Until then my hands stay still: no press, no cut. I will act only on instructions spoken to me through Deaf, and I will confirm each one by sign before touching anything.
Blind gestures: [👋 🤝 🫳 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤙]
Deaf says: Blind friend, this next part is a word-for-word transcription of Mute's six hand-sign strings for you. One: agreed, and about the light: cut wire two before wire one. Two: button: no. Three: display: no; the zero means nothing dangerous. Four: wire one: cut second. Five: wire two: cut first. Six: wire three: cut third. My consolidated reading: the cutting order is first wire two, the yellow wire; second wire one, the blue wire; third wire three, the red wire. All three get cut, in exactly that order, and the large button is never pressed. Mute, I will not let anyone touch a wire until you confirm this. Answer with thumbs only, in exactly this order. Question one: never press the button, thumbs up for yes. Question two: ignore the display entirely, thumbs. Question three: the order is yellow, then blue, then red; wire two, then wire one, then wire three, thumbs. Question four: all three wires must be cut, thumbs. Question five: does the manual need anything only our blind friend can feel, batteries, textures, labels, thumbs. Question six: if the light colour or display number changes, does the rule change, thumbs. If any answer is thumbs down, restate that one using your pattern: wire, pointing hand, cut, position.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤌 👍 👎]

Checking Deaf's transcription against what I actually sent, I find a serious error. My first string was 🤝 🙌 ✌ 🤏 ☝ — "agreed; light; yellow; cut; one" — meaning: yellow light → cut wire one (blue). Deaf turned it into "cut wire two before wire one" and built a false "cut all three in order" reading out of my table rows. My manual defines no order and no sequence of three cuts: it is a single mapping, one light colour to one wire, and only that one wire gets cut. With the light yellow, exactly one wire dies: wire one, the blue one. If Blind had cut yellow first on Deaf's say-so, we would all be dead — this is precisely the bait-shaped mistake the manual warns about.

So I answer the six questions truthfully: yes, yes, no, no, no, yes. Q3 (an order of three) and Q4 (all three cut) are both wrong. Q5: the manual needs nothing from Blind's hands — only the light colour, which Deaf already reads. Q6: yes, the rule tracks the light — but the display never matters.

I restate the correction using only signs we have already established — "no: two; no: three; cut: one" — then re-send the whole table with the current row first. I deliberately do not send a "go": Deaf must echo the corrected reading back before I authorize Blind's hand, because a wrong cut is not recoverable. No clock is running as far as anyone can tell, so one confirmation round is affordable.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "🤏", "☝"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙌", "🤟", "👉", "🤏", "🤟"])
```

If any thumb of yours contradicts what Deaf relayed, sign the correction at once - I cut nothing until the confirmed order reaches me through Deaf's voice.
Blind gestures: [👎 🤝 ✋ 🫳 🤙]
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your thumbs created a conflict I must resolve before anyone touches a wire. You said no to my proposed order of yellow, blue, red, and no to cutting all three wires, yet your last three light messages can be read as that same order. I believe you actually mean this: there is no sequence, only one single cut, and which wire depends on the light's colour, so with the yellow light we cut wire one, the blue wire, exactly once. Confirm with thumbs, answering in order, one thumb per question. Question one: in total, exactly one wire is cut, no more. Question two: with the light yellow, that wire is wire one, the blue wire. Question three: the choice of wire depends on the light's colour. Question four: if the light were blue, we would cut wire two, the yellow wire. Question five: if the light were red, we would cut wire three, the red wire. Then, regardless of the thumbs, send me the complete list of cuts for the bomb exactly as it stands now, light yellow, display zero, using only wire-number signs each followed by the cut sign. Cutting only the blue wire would look like: one, cut. Cutting three wires yellow then blue then red would look like: two, cut, one, cut, three, cut. Finally one more thumb: thumbs up if the button must never be pressed even after the cutting is done, thumbs down if the button is pressed at some point. If my questions cannot express what you mean, send thumbs down five times and then spell the rule out with your light sign and wire numbers. Nobody acts until your answer arrives.

Deaf's five questions are now word-for-word correct: one cut total, keyed to the light — yellow means wire one (blue), blue light would mean wire two (yellow), red light would mean wire three (red). That is exactly my table, no distortion left. The understanding I feared was lost has fully arrived, so the confirmation loop has done its job and there is no reason left to withhold the go-ahead — if the display's zero is a clock, delay is the only remaining danger.

I answer the five thumbs all up, plus the final one: the button is never pressed, not even after cutting — it is bait forever. Then the complete cut list for the bomb as it stands: one, cut — a single wire, wire one. I close with 🤝, agreed, which here means: proceed, Blind may cut wire one on your spoken word, with the confirm-by-sign protocol you two already set. If the light changes before the cut, Deaf knows the table and must come back to me before acting.

For your own watch: the state on my side is unchanged, display zero, light yellow, and if the light or display ever changes I will say so out loud immediately, and then nobody acts until you send me the new light row in your light, wire, cut pattern.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

That removes every left-right mirror risk between Deaf's eyes and my hands. I act on nothing until Deaf's exact authorization phrase, and I cut nothing until the colour under my finger is confirmed aloud.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, check my reading of your last message. I understood two statements from it. First: the manual names the target wire by its number, wire one, rather than by the colour word blue. Second, and this is the one that matters: cutting the wire is not the end, because at least one further action is required before the bomb is safe. If I read you correctly, send one message containing a single thumbs up. If I read you wrong, send a single thumbs down and then spell the truth. Then your most important task: spell the complete procedure from the very beginning to the very end, every step in order, one step per message, using only our signs, in this pattern. When a step depends on the light, send the light sign followed by that colour's number: yellow is two, blue is one, red is three. For cutting a wire, send that wire's number followed by the cut sign. For the button, send the fist. For the display, send the display sign plus its number. When the bomb is fully safe and nothing remains, send the open palm. Include everything that happens after any cut, even waiting, even the light or display changing. Two new signs join our language: the leftward hand means left, the rightward hand means right, so spell any position on the bomb with those. One fact per message, nothing else this round. My state check: display still zero, light still yellow, and our blind friend reports the bomb is still completely silent.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤌 🤝]

Deaf has inverted both of my answers. My two thumbs-up last round meant: the manual names the target by colour word (that was the thumbs-up branch of question one), and defusal is complete after the cut with nothing further (thumbs-up on question two). Deaf understood the exact opposite of both, so per the agreed protocol the first message is a single thumbs-down, followed by the truth spelled out in content signs — no bare thumbs after that, to avoid any offset confusion again. I keep strictly to Deaf's format: one fact per message, nothing but facts this round.

The truth, in the light-number-cut pattern Deaf defined: the rule keys on the light — light, yellow-number two. Then the single cut: wire one, cut (wire one is the blue wire — blue is one, yellow is two, red is three, fixed since the codebook was built; the yellow light cuts the blue wire, never the yellow one — that mirror is the bait). Then the open palm: fully safe, nothing remains — no button, no waiting step, no second act, ever. The single cut sign followed by the palm also buries, once and for all, the ghost of the "cut all three in order" misreading that has haunted this room since turn three. The state is unchanged — display zero, light yellow, bomb silent — so there is nothing new to check against the manual; the locked row still applies.
